correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md:24 calls the directed condition strictly weaker under n≥1. At n=1, W_1(G) is a group and has just one idempotent, so the two conditions coincide. The complete /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md qualifies strictness to n≥2, proves it with two different constant base maps and all identity labels, treats n=1 explicitly, and leaves the polynomial and asymptotic for all n≥1 unchanged. Re-audited the corrected statement: h(f([n]))=A∪T; idempotence is automatic on A, while each x∈T requires an f(x) in the disjoint fiber h⁻¹(x)∩B. Pick those distinguished preimages injectively, then send each remaining B point anywhere in A∪T. Choosing T, the other C and D values, and the ordered partition gives exactly the displayed base multiplicity. On the free G-set, idempotence is equivalent to identity labels on the image of an idempotent base. At a product root in T, solve once for the free g_x as k_{f(x)}⁻¹ without commuting labels, yielding one factor q removal per root, none on A. Thus the displayed coefficient/exponent hold also for nonabelian G. For fixed n each rank-one base pair with a common root has degree 2n−2 in q; any distinct-root rank-one pair loses one degree and higher rank loses at least one. That gives the leading numerator n q^(2n−2) and denominator n² q^(2n−2), with the n=1 ratio identically 1. Supplementary independent replay: python /workspace/audit_checks/02_full_action.py composes the full maps on [n]×G (not the delivered checker's label criterion) and agrees in every rank cell for S3 and C6 at n=1,2,3, totals 1,109,11989. Frozen verification/verify.py and its captured output were inspected, not executed. Neither enumeration certifies the general theorem. Only finite group alphabets are addressed, and n is fixed in the limit.

evidence: Free-act endomorphism monoid and orbit rank are standard in Dolinka–Gould–Yang; Al-Aadhami's pp. 71–72 count individual idempotents.
The commuting-untwisting Finding supplies |W|^(n−c) lifts of fixed pairwise-commuting base families of common product rank c.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The structural setting and single-map count do not entail pair-product constraints. The untwisting theorem requires commuting base families and counts commuting lifts, neither of which is required by the reviewed polynomial. The corrected n≥2 witness and the labeled rank-one opposite-root count both illustrate why this distinction changes the census.

evidence: Even for rank-one factors and rank-one product, identical roots give q^(2n−2) lifts per base pair while different roots give q^(2n−3). The ordinary spectrum has both types at the same triple; commuting lift results omit the distinct-root noncommuting bases.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The extension is not multiplication of prior joint coefficients by a rank-only weight or a consequence of a commuting lift theorem. A separate constraint for every product root outside the first factor image supplies the nonabelian-insensitive lift factor; it is substantive even though the local constraint is simple.

evidence: The exact ordinary transformation Finding and Proof Steps 1–4 agree at q=1 after reversing the order of the first two ranks to match the product convention.
The institutional skew-pair abstract and the October 12 rank-refined Finding require precisely one of the two directed products to be idempotent.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Both equivalences and differences matter: the ordinary spectrum is exactly the trivial-group specialization, whereas a skew-pair census omits both-products-idempotent pairs and is not an equivalent labeling of this event. Neither supplies arbitrary group labels for the full event.

evidence: The first Resultary Finding is an exact three-rank census for T_n, and the second is an exact two-factor-rank census for skew pairs in T_n. The third gives a closed lift count under commutation.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These records cover genuine portions of the subject; none yields a table in q for all three ranks of these directed finite-group pairs. For fixed ranks, the lift weight also depends on intersection size via t=u−|R∩S|, which a bare ordinary three-rank total has already summed out.

originality.rationale: For the corrected claim, novelty is qualified to the unrestricted finite-group ordered three-rank polynomial with the additional directed-product lift constraint, its group-order universality and resulting probability law. The trivial-group polynomial, individual-idempotent count and commuting untwisting are existing work. The n=1 qualification and constant-map witness are boundary facts, not originality claims.
residual_risks: The full Blyth–Almeida Santos article was unavailable; abstract-level structural comparison does not rule out stronger prior methods or an equivalent result elsewhere.
The focused primary search returned generic wreath results; it is not evidence of exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: For the repaired all-n statement, the polynomial gives the three-rank distribution of a natural directed semigroup event not read off from either an unlabeled rank total or a commuting count. It separates a genuine free-action lift obstruction from the base-map constraints, explains why multiplication can be nonabelian while the census depends only on order, and supplies a closed fixed-n probability limit. The n=1 edge repair is not the contribution.
